goal: Review the current Promptcraft implementation and uncommitted diff for correctness as an intent translator and harness-dialect compiler; identify material defects or semantic-assurance gaps with source-linked evidence.
allowed_effects: read repository files and git diff
run existing read-only tests and static checks
write only the final response to the controller-provided output path
forbidden_effects: commit, push, merge, deploy, or release
production, Plan Vault, flake.nix, marketplace, credential, or external effects
requirements: Inspect promptcraft/core.py, promptcraft/server.py, promptcraft/cli.py, tests/test_promptcraft.py, bin/labctl.py, schemas/run-manifest.schema.json, promptcraft/README.md, README.md, and ROUTING.md
Inspect the current git diff so staged and uncommitted candidate behavior is included
Check whether intent_sha256 truly remains receiver-independent while dialect_sha256 captures receiver-specific strategy
Check receipt compatibility and whether labctl binds the exact PASS prompt safely
Check MCP prompt handling, draft-as-data boundaries, and accidental execution or authority leakage
Run the existing unit tests and deterministic checks permitted by the read-only sandbox
Distinguish confirmed defects, design limitations, and future enhancements
non_goals: Do not redesign unrelated Capability Lab components
Do not treat stylistic preference as a defect
acceptance_checks: Every finding names an exact file and stable line range or symbol
Each finding states severity, consequence, and the smallest justified correction
Test claims quote the command and observed result
If no material defect is found, say so directly without inventing one
